classification_rationale: Pilot candidate after manual source-check review: one explicit global command is testable by exact line presence, but model/software support and STP-mode applicability remain unverified.
remediation: Review platform/software support and topology requirements, then enable STP Loop Guard through the approved change process: spanning-tree loopguard default.
review_notes: Pilot candidate only. The source Check explicitly names one global command.
The source title says STP Loop Guard must be enabled, but command support and interaction with the deployed STP mode must be verified for each target family and software release.
Do not approve for execution until applicability is verified. Synthetic positive/negative fixtures are maintained under tests/fixtures/stig/cisco_ios/batch_01.
source_check_text:
Review the switch configuration to verify that STP Loop Guard is enabled as shown in the configuration example below:

hostname SW2
…
…
…
spanning-tree mode pvst
spanning-tree loopguard default

If STP Loop Guard is not enabled, this is a finding.
source_fix_text: Configure the switch to have STP Loop Guard enabled via the spanning-tree loopguard default global command.
title: The Cisco switch must have Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) Loop Guard enabled.
